surreptitious, furtive
избегающий откровенности, не рассказывающий другим о себе

examples.text: Иванов был всегда скрытным, угрюмым человеком.

glosses: simple past and past participle of reserve
Slow to reveal emotion or opinions.

examples.text: He was a quiet, reserved person.

glosses: Set aside for a particular person or purpose; spoken for.

examples.text: I'm sorry, sir, but these are reserved seats.

glosses: Unwilling to communicate; keeping one's thoughts and opinions to oneself; reserved or restrained.

examples.text: They are slow and reticent, and are like a dull good horse which lets every nag pass him, but with whip and spur will run down every racer in the field.

But he was a reticent as well as an eccentric man; and he made no mention of a certain evening when he warmed his hands at the gatehouse fire, and looked steadily down upon a certain heap of torn and miry clothes upon the floor.
She had told him she was not now at Marlott, but had been curiously reticent as to her actual address, and the only course was to go to Marlott and inquire for it.

The inhabitants of that street impressed me peculiarly; At first I thought it was because they were all silent and reticent; but later decided it was because they were all very old.
But they were not reticent enough to prevent the circulation of certain uneasy rumours and extravagant stories of discreditable adventures.

glosses: Hesitant or not wanting to take some action; reluctant (usually followed by a verb in the infinitive).

examples.text: One letter from Deborah presents an especially fascinating contrast with Jane's letters to her brother. Whereas Jane was keen on discussing politics, Deborah was reticent to do so.

While many uncomfortable components of the Holocaust have been analyzed in minute detail, the rape of Jewish women during this era persists as a subject that scholars and victims alike are reticent to explore.

As I suggested at the outset, this claim regarding Derrida’s relation to the Greeks is one that Derrida himself would have been reticent to accept.
The police may be reticent to charge the alleged offender, prosecutors reticent to continue with the prosecution, and juries reticent to convict.

glosses: Having an inclination to secrecy.

examples.text: She's a secretive girl, not giving away much about her life.

glosses: Qui n’est pas ouvert.

examples.text: Quand Ampère a étudié expérimentalement les actions mutuelles des courants, il n’a opéré et il ne pouvait opérer que sur des courants fermés.

glosses: En parlant d'un visage, qui n'exprime aucune émotion, sinon de la rancœur.

examples.text: Étant donné qu'il n'y avait pas de taxi dans les parages, nous sommes revenus à pied, moi portant le petit, la marraine suivant derrière, le visage soudain fermé comme une porte de prison.

glosses: Qualifie une partie d'un espace topologique dont le complémentaire est ouvert. Pour un espace métrique, qui est clos par limites de suites.
Se dit d'une courbe ou plus généralement d'une variété qui est compacte.

examples.text: Théorème de Jordan : toute courbe fermée simple du plan sépare ce dernier en deux composantes.

glosses: Complémentaire d’un ouvert.

examples.text: J’ai fermé la maison et je suis monté dans la Volvo.

glosses: Qui ne laisse pas apercevoir ses sentiments, ses desseins.

examples.text: J’ai affaire à un de ces hommes adroits, aimables, et profondément dissimulés, que l’on voit dans les romans. Ils savent plaire, mais précisément parce qu’ils sont incapables d’aimer.
